task.description: Diagnose the call-graph shape of ISS-0512's async:true-reaches-Sandbox.mode/2 defect class and recommend a detection strategy for CODE-DESIGNER.

result.note:
STEP 0.5 REGISTRY LOOKUP: ISS-0113 (resolved WF03-ISS0423-20260905) and ISS-0480 (still open, unrelated mechanism -- see below) are the two prior entries. ISS-0113's resolution is the load-bearing fact for this issue: `TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1`'s own unconditional first line, `Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto)`, was DELIBERATELY KEPT (not removed) as the mechanism that makes async:true safe for a call site, PROVIDED that call site is independently verified against 3 failure mechanisms (self-checkout, concurrent multi-process DB access, second provisioning call) documented in lib/letflow/design/iss0113-tenant-fixture-sandbox-restore-opt-in.md section 9. Only 2 of 46 real call sites (secrets_test.exs, webhooks_test.exs) were ever converted+verified; the other 44 remain async:false. This is NOT itself a bug -- the risk ISS-0512 exists to guard against is a FUTURE async:true conversion (of one of those 44, or a brand-new test file) that calls provisioned_tenant!/1 (or any other function reaching mode/2) WITHOUT going through that verification procedure. This is the third recurrence of the general class (ISS-0113 flagged the risk in prose only; ISS-0480 turned out to be a DIFFERENT, unrelated mechanism -- a load-dependent Sandbox checkout race on plain async:true DataCase tests, `test/letflow/row_approval_test.exs` and `test/letflow/definitions/pack_update_migration_test.exs`, NEITHER of which calls provisioned_tenant!/1 or any TenantFixture code at all; confirmed by reading both files in full -- so ISS-0480 is cross-referenced by the issue filer but is not evidence of the transitive-reach mechanism itself, only evidence sandbox fragility in this codebase is a recurring theme). No fix has previously been attempted for THIS specific defect class (a static/mechanical guard); severity stands at MAJOR as filed, not escalated further since nothing has actually recurred in the sense of a broken guard -- there is no guard yet to break.

DIRECT mode/2 (or Sandbox.mode) CALL SITES found by `grep -rn 'Sandbox\.mode' test/support/`:
- test/support/tenant_fixture.ex:222 -- inside `provisioned_tenant!/1`, unconditional first statement. THIS IS THE ONE the issue is about.
- test/support/tenant_schema_reaper.ex:150, :202, :225, :273 -- inside private helpers of `sweep_orphans/2` (called from test/test_helper.exs before ExUnit.start() and via ExUnit.after_suite/1 -- i.e. from `test_helper.exs`, never from inside a running test's process, and never from a module compiled as a test case at all).
- test/support/tenant_template.ex:82 -- inside `ensure_template!/0`, called by `provisioned_tenant!/1` on the `template: :clone` (default) path AND directly by some test files. Comment at tenant_template.ex line ~78-81 explicitly notes: 'tenant_fixture.ex's provisioned_tenant!/1 already sets :auto before it reaches here... Setting it here is idempotent.'

CALL CHAIN FROM `TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1` -- CONFIRMED, not inferred: read test/support/tenant_fixture.ec:220-248 in full. Line 222, the function's own literal first statement, is `Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto)`. This is a DIRECT call, zero hops -- not merely 'transitively reachable', it IS the mode/2 call site. The 'transitive' framing in the issue text refers to a TEST FILE reaching it: a test file that merely calls `TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1` (1 hop) reaches mode/2 without ever writing `Sandbox.mode` itself. provisioned_tenant!/1 additionally calls (2nd hop, only on the default `template: :clone` path) `Letflow.Test.TenantTemplate.ensure_template!/0`, which is ALSO a direct mode/2 caller (tenant_template.ex:82) -- so on the default path a calling test reaches mode/2 via TWO independent direct call sites in the same call, not one.

ASYNC:TRUE TEST FILES SURVEYED -- `grep -rnE 'use +[A-Za-z0-9_.]+, *async: *true' test/ --include=*.exs` (anchored on a real `use ... async: true` declaration line, per the issue's own caution) found 60 real declarations across test/. Cross-referencing against every file that mentions `provisioned_tenant!` anywhere (`grep -rl provisioned_tenant! test/`) via `comm -12` on the sorted file lists gives 3 candidate overlaps: test/letflow/secrets_test.exs, test/letflow/webhooks_test.exs, test/letflow/routers/mobile_tenant_config_test.exs. Manual inspection of each candidate's actual call sites (not just the filename-level grep hit) is where the issue's own caution about naive detection bites on the CALLER side too, not just the async:true side: mobile_tenant_config_test.exs's only occurrence of the string `provisioned_tenant!` (line 13) is inside its OWN moduledoc, contrasting itself with identity_test.exs's use of the fixture -- it does NOT call the fixture; its moduledoc explicitly states 'no Letflow.TenantFixture schema-provisioning/... machinery is needed here' and the file only touches the global `tenants` table via plain Letflow.DataCase. Confirmed by grep restricted to non-comment executable lines: zero real calls. The other two, secrets_test.exs (line 44) and webhooks_test.exs (line 47), DO have real executable call-site lines (`Letflow.TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!(` starting a real function call, not inside a doc string) in addition to their own moduledoc prose about the fixture -- confirmed genuine. These are exactly ISS-0113's 2 verified-safe conversions; both currently comply with the invariant (they were the ones the 3-mechanism procedure was run against). CONCLUSION: as of this commit, zero async:true test files reach mode/2 in an UNVERIFIED way -- the invariant currently holds by luck/discipline, not by any mechanical guard, which is exactly the gap ISS-0512 exists to close. Additionally checked ISS-0480's two named files (row_approval_test.exs, pack_update_migration_test.exs, both async:true via Letflow.DataCase) for any TenantFixture/mode(2) involvement: neither calls provisioned_tenant!/1, ensure_template!/0, or Sandbox.mode directly anywhere in the file (confirmed by full read + grep) -- their failure mode is unrelated to this defect class.

FEASIBILITY OF STATIC DETECTION -- concrete scope: YES, feasible as a BOUNDED, SUPPORT-MODULE-ONLY call-graph walk, NOT general Elixir static analysis. Concretely: (1) Enumerate test/**/*_test.exs files; for each, scan for a line matching an anchored regex for a real declaration, e.g. `^\s*use\s+[A-Za-z0-9_.]+\s*,.*async:\s*true` (must reject a bare `async: true` appearing inside a `@moduledoc`/`#` comment/backtick-quoted prose -- the issue's own caution; a line-based regex anchored to `use` as the first non-whitespace token, ignoring lines inside `""".."""` heredocs and `#` comments, handles this cleanly since Elixir test files always declare `use ExUnit.Case`/`use Letflow.DataCase` as a real top-level statement, and a moduledoc heredoc block is trivially detectable by tracking `@moduledoc """` / closing `"""` state while scanning line-by-line). (2) For each async:true file, extract its `alias`/fully-qualified calls into a small fixed allowlist of KNOWN support modules that are reachable call sites for this defect class: `Letflow.TenantFixture`, `Letflow.Test.TenantTemplate`, `Letflow.TenantSchemaReaper`, and any bare `Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.mode(` / `Sandbox.mode(` occurring directly in the test file itself. This allowlist is SMALL and CLOSED because it is exactly the module list already established: TenantFixture and TenantTemplate are the only test/support/ modules containing a mode/2 call reachable from a live test process (TenantSchemaReaper's mode/2 calls run only from test_helper.exs, pre-ExUnit-start / after_suite, never from within a running test -- see 'legitimate callers' below, but a checker can still statically verify a test file never calls into TenantSchemaReaper's public function directly, since none currently do and doing so would be its own new hazard). (3) Build a tiny, hardcoded 2-level call graph, not a general one: `TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1` -> (unconditionally) `Sandbox.mode/2`, and -> (conditionally, `template: :clone` default) -> `TenantTemplate.ensure_template!/0` -> `Sandbox.mode/2`. A checker does not need to interpret the `template:` option's runtime value -- it should conservatively treat ANY call to `provisioned_tenant!/1` as reaching mode/2 regardless of opts (the conditional path is still the default, and static analysis of keyword-list contents to prove the non-default `:replay` path is used is not worth the complexity for 2 known call sites). (4) A call is 'real' if it appears as `Letflow.TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!(` or (given a matching `alias Letflow.TenantFixture` line) a bare `provisioned_tenant!(` call, OUTSIDE any `@moduledoc`/comment/heredoc span -- same heredoc-tracking technique as step 1. WHAT NOT TO ATTEMPT: general reachability through `import`, dynamic `apply/3`/`Kernel.apply`, macros that generate calls, or following into arbitrary application code (e.g. if some `lib/letflow/` helper someday itself called Sandbox.mode -- none currently do, grep of `lib/` for `Sandbox.mode` returned zero hits, only design-doc markdown mentions) -- a full Elixir call-graph analyzer is out of proportion to a 2-module, 1-function allowlist and would itself become a maintenance burden bigger than the defect it guards against. If a genuinely new test/support/ module is added later that calls mode/2, the checker's allowlist itself needs a deliberate update (this is an acceptable, auditable limitation to state explicitly in the design, not something to solve generically).

LEGITIMATE (must-not-flag) mode/2 CALLERS, why: test/support/tenant_schema_reaper.ex's 4 call sites (lines 150, 202, 225, 273) run ONLY inside `sweep_orphans/2`'s private helpers, which are invoked exclusively from test/test_helper.exs (once before `ExUnit.start()`, once via `ExUnit.after_suite/1`) -- i.e. never from inside any test module's own process, never from a module that itself is a compiled ExUnit test case, and structurally incapable of racing a concurrently-running async test because both invocation points are OUTSIDE ExUnit's test-execution window entirely (before any test starts, or after every test has already finished). test/support/tenant_template.ex's single call site (line 82, inside `ensure_template!/0`) is legitimate PRECISELY BECAUSE it is the one deliberately-accepted mode/2 call that async:true call sites are allowed to transitively reach (per ISS-0113's resolution) -- the file itself is not a test file (no `use ExUnit.Case`/`use Letflow.DataCase`, no test/1 blocks; grep confirms it has neither), so it is never itself the SUBJECT of the async:true check, only a support module the check's call graph passes through. Neither file should be flagged BY VIRTUE OF DECLARING async:true (they don't declare it at all -- both are plain modules, not ExUnit cases) -- the acceptance criterion 'not false-flagged' is trivially satisfiable by scoping the checker's file-selection step to only files containing a real `use ... , async: true` line, since neither support file has one.

WHERE `mix letflow.check`'s CHAIN IS DEFINED: mix.exs, `aliases/0`, the `"letflow.check":` key (currently mix.exs lines ~91-108). Current order: `letflow.check_toolchain` -> `letflow.check_requirements_registration` -> `letflow.check_deferral_staleness` -> `letflow.lint_handoffs` -> `format --check-formatted` -> `compile --warnings-as-errors` -> `letflow.check.test`. Each check is its own `Mix.Tasks.Letflow.*` module under lib/mix/tasks/letflow.*.ex (e.g. lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check_toolchain.ex, lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check_requirements_registration.ex, lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check_deferral_staleness.ex, lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex), each following the same pattern: a `Mix.Tasks.Letflow.CheckXxx` module implementing `run/1`, calling `Mix.raise/1` (or exiting non-zero) on failure, with its own moduledoc stating explicitly which alias slot it occupies and why (e.g. check_deferral_staleness.ex's moduledoc states it is positioned 'immediately after the registration check... shares a parse of docs/requirements.yaml'). A new check for ISS-0512 (e.g. `Mix.Tasks.Letflow.CheckAsyncSandboxReachability` or similar) should follow this exact pattern: new module under lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check_async_sandbox_reachability.ex (or similar name), a new `"letflow.check_async_sandbox_reachability"` entry added to the `letflow.check` alias list in mix.exs. Positioning candidate: it is a pure static/textual analysis over test/ source (like letflow.lint_handoffs and letflow.check_requirements_registration, both of which parse repo files without compiling/running anything), so it belongs alongside those fast, non-compiling checks -- BEFORE `compile --warnings-as-errors` and `letflow.check.test`, and does not need to run after any particular other check (no shared parse target with the existing ones). CODE-DESIGNER should confirm exact placement and naming but has everything needed here to do so without re-diagnosing.

REGRESSION-TEST HOOK FOR STEP 4 (informational, not this step's job to design): a fail-then-pass regression test for the eventual fix must (a) prove the checker passes today (0 async:true files reach mode/2, as established above) and (b) prove it FAILS if a new/modified async:true test file is made to call provisioned_tenant!/1 (or a fixture wrapping it) -- e.g. by adding a throwaway fixture file under a temp test-scan directory the checker is pointed at, not by actually breaking a real test file in the tree.
